newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent crude cargoes heard traded lower.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent crude cargoes heard traded lower.

text.p: Two cargoes of Brent crude due to load around the end of February were heard to have been sold on Monday well below Friday's traded level, traders said.

The cargoes - both February 26-28 loaders were heard to have been sold to two refiners at March Brent -27 cents and -27.5 cents, down from Friday's deal at March -20 cents. With many traders away from their offices at industry functions the deals could not be immediately confirmed, but traders saw these as market levels.
"That's about where the Brent is and I believe they were both done," one commented.
The two March 4-6 Brents due to turn wet on Monday were still being passed through the paper chains.
The March 2-4 cargo which was thought on Friday to have been defered was now heard brought forward and will load at the end of February.
Brent paper markets were very quiet. Intermonth spreads were discussed around +30/33 for March/April, 23/30 for April/May and 20/27 for May/June.
Action on CFD's was similarly thin with next week (Feb 24-28) talked around April Brent +10/14 cents and the roll into Feb 17-21 heard valued around -3 cents.
Berthing at Sullom Voe terminal was suspended on Sunday due to high winds which were expected to continue into Tuesday.

Crude loadings at Statfjord and Gullfaks were also halted on Monday due to hurricane-force winds. So far production at both fields was normal, operator Statoil said, but output at the Statfjord C platform would be reduced to a minimum at 0200 GMT on Tuesday due to lack of storage capacity.
Production resumed at the Norwegian Ekofisk field following a brief shutdown while a section of pipeline was repaired.
